clue.text: Following report of communist, letters must show these

parts.note: post- as a prefix means after or following

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word that follows is to be said aloud

parts.note: Karl Marx, founder of communism

explanation.surface: A political demand that mail must display something, following word from a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: The communist is Marx, whose name sounds the same as MARKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Every posted envelope carries a postmark, the stamp showing where and when it was sent.

clue.text: See 22 across
Perhaps Victoria is not at fault

indicators.note: the 'at' of 'at fault' doubles as fodder, so fault alone says the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that Queen Victoria is blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen of the puzzle's royal theme, but she is the London railway terminus. The 'at' of 'at fault' is shared by fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a major London railway terminus, an example of a station, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Unwashed masses taking king's head

indicators.note: taking means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the masses are the many, the common people

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The great unwashed public seize the king's head in revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwashed masses' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after 'Unwashed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manky is British slang for dirty or grubby, which fits something left unwashed.

clue.text: Alfred: he atoned partly for the result of a fire

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: King Alfred, who famously burnt the cakes, made amends for the damage his fire caused.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire heats metal or coals until they glow red, so red heat is what a fire produces.

clue.text: Snack in foil, say pig's foot

parts.note: to foil a plan is to scotch it
say means for example, EG

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A snack wrapped in foil, for instance a pig's trotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen wrapping but is the verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg, a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, is a popular British picnic snack.

clue.text: Suffer no fool: Canute misquoted about heresy, initially

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the next piece
a misquoted saying has its words wrongly arranged, so the remaining letters are shuffled
no says the word for fool is taken away from the name

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person, a fool

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: King Canute, who would not tolerate fools, is misreported on the subject of heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes the fool out first, leaving CAE; 'misquoted' makes that ACE, and 'about' wraps it round the initial of heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel a dull pain, to suffer.

clue.text: Edward, our sovereign, showed passions

indicators.note: showed says the answer is displayed within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: King Edward displayed strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardours are intense feelings of enthusiasm or love, so a plural for passions.

clue.text: King, to be beheaded, takes sanctuary somewhere near Wembley

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter of the name, as Charles I lost his head

parts.note: Charles is a king's name
a den is a private retreat, a sanctuary

explanation.surface: A doomed king takes refuge in a place near Wembley.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I really was beheaded, so the instruction doubles as history. HARLESDEN is a district of northwest London, a short way from Wembley.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlesden lies in the London borough of Brent, which also contains Wembley.

clue.text: Decreed: set gold before man of the North, reported journalist

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: reported means the word is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a Dane comes from Denmark, a northern people
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper item ordering gold to be laid before a Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order officially, so ordained means decreed.

clue.text: Old heartless Richard III in feud about filth

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving only the ends of the name
III in means the third letter of the following word

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A historical picture of a cruel Richard III wallowing in filth during a family feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Richard III' looks like the king, but III belongs with 'in feud', picking its third letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordure is excrement, dung, hence filth.

clue.text: Stand for leadership of the youth party in free Yugoslavia

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Tito-era politics: the youth party leaders standing for office in a free Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: To typify is to be a typical example of, to represent or stand for.

clue.text: Gave out (caught), left in, left out

indicators.note: in means the two letters are placed inside the word for gave out

parts.note: to exude is to give out or emit
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: a batsman given out caught, another left in, someone left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude is to leave someone out, so excluded means left out.

clue.text: Way a man embraces a queen

indicators.note: embraces means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: Mr is the title of a man
Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A description of how a man hugs a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer ends in ER, tempting a solver to read 'queen' as the usual ER; here the queen is a named one, embraced by the man's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is the way something is done.

clue.text: Oh, I parted sadly from love's image

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lover's lament: 'Oh, I parted from you in sorrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love, its personification or image.

clue.text: Exercising restraint, as the Queen is said to do in spirit

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: what the Queen does, as monarch, is reign
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A remark that the Queen holds herself back, in spirit at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Reining in a horse pulls it back, so the phrase means holding back or restraining.

clue.text: Renovated seediest part of the North

indicators.note: renovated means made over, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Regeneration of the most run-down area of northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: TEESSIDE is the area around the River Tees in northeast England, once heavy industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside is a region of northeast England, a part of the North.

clue.text: As at first, Henry VIII was intellectual

parts.note: Henry VIII grew famously fat, but as a young man he was slim
Henry VIII was a king

explanation.surface: A claim that Henry VIII began as a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII grew obese later in life; as a young man he was a THIN KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking describes a person given to reasoning, an intellectual sort.

clue.text: More unpleasant than retsina? Unlikely!

indicators.note: unlikely signals the letters are put in an improbable new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wine-taster asks whether anything tastes worse than Greek retsina, and doubts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, so more unpleasant.

clue.text: Getting bigger, King George: one defined by his appetite?

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's cypher
an eater is someone known for how much they eat

explanation.surface: A fattening King George, known mainly for his gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is a link: the definition is 'bigger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is the comparative of great, meaning larger.

clue.text: In Scotland's valleys, Elizabeth's heart picks up

indicators.note: In means the letter goes inside the valleys

parts.note: a glen is a Scottish valley

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A queen's affection is collected in the Highland valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, to pick up.

clue.text: Boatman placed between noble and royal persons previously

indicators.note: placed between means the setter's letter sits between the two other pieces

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for either Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: The setter finds himself seated between aristocrats and royalty at some past event.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter, so he is I. ER stands for 'persons' because two Queen Elizabeths have used it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, previously.

clue.text: Plot to murder princes about nothing

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the zero
to murder is to mangle, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A scheme to kill princes, perhaps the Princes in the Tower, over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to scheme together, to plot.

clue.text: Terrible danger, with political activists at Buckingham House event

indicators.note: terrible implies mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a political party is made up of activists

explanation.surface: Protesters at Buckingham Palace pose a dreadful threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckingham House was the original name of Buckingham Palace, where the monarch hosts garden parties every summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal garden parties are held in the grounds of Buckingham Palace, once Buckingham House.

clue.text: Harold at first confessed rising up to snap in anger

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: King Harold confessing a rebellion, then lashing out in fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash the teeth is to grind or snap them together angrily.

clue.text: Good to leave the upper class no way out

indicators.note: to leave says that letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: the gentry are the upper class

explanation.surface: Decent people abandoning the aristocracy find themselves trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no way out' sounds like a trap, but it simply means a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an entrance, the opposite of an exit, so not a way out.

clue.text: Man of the North, as James I was in Scotland!

parts.note: James I of England had already been James VI of Scotland, the sixth
James I was a king

explanation.surface: A boast that King James was a true northerner when ruling Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: James I of England was the sixth James to rule Scotland, so there he was a VI KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were Scandinavian seafarers, men from the far North.

clue.text: Boatman, at heart European, in first part of Tory attack

indicators.note: at heart means the letter sits in the middle of the sailor

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a man of boats
the opening two letters of the word Tory

explanation.surface: The setter, a European at heart, joins in the early part of a Conservative assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlike 20 down, Boatman here is TAR, a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to attack them fiercely, verbally or physically.

clue.text: Charles broadcast to listeners?

indicators.note: to listeners means as heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A question whether Prince Charles was on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: At the time Charles was heir to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Charles was for decades the heir apparent to the British throne.

clue.text: Lorry then diverted in the direction of Scotland?

indicators.note: a diverted lorry takes a new route, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A lorry rerouted towards Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies to the north of England, so going northerly is heading that way.
